newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Black Sea states vow to boost trade links.
newsitem.headline: Black Sea states vow to boost trade links.

text.p: Countries ringing the Black Sea vowed on Friday to boost trade links and to step up cooperation in energy, transport, trade financing, communications and tourism.

In a declaration issued during a one-day meeting in Moscow, the 11 member states of the Black Sea Cooperation forum also promised to work together to fight organised crime, terrorism and illegal trade in drugs and arms.
"We have come to the conclusion that the forum is developing positively and has a good future," Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin told a news conference after the meeting.
"We agreed to examine the possibility of extending trade benefits to each other."
The forum supported peace initiatives in the Balkans and the Caucasus, where the meeting's host country Russia has agreed a truce with separatists in its breakaway Chechnya region.
"The Black Sea is a sea of success, a sea of prosperity, a sea of peace and a sea of stability," Turkish President Suleyman Demirel told the same conference.
The forum groups Russia, Turkey, Greece, Ukraine, Romania, Bulgaria, Moldova, Albania, Armenia, Azerbaijan and Georgia. Its next half-yearly meeting will be held in Turkey.
